Definition: a pit hole (especially one used as a cistern or a prison)
BiblicalUsage: A pit is the word for a hole in the ground, a cistern, a prison — and it appears sixty-two times. In Genesis 37:20 Joseph's brothers say, come, let us slay him, and cast him into some pit. In Psalms 40:2 David says, he brought me up also out of an horrible pit, out of the miry clay, and set my feet upon a rock. And in Jeremiah 38:6 they take Jeremiah and cast him into the dungeon of Malchiah, and Jeremiah sinks down in the mire.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the pit in the Psalms is the promise for every pit: he brought me up out of it, and set my feet upon a rock — and he does the same for me.
